args.title: E5: pure-ordering primitive in ewe v1
args.subject: q:ewe-E5-pure-ordering

args.text: The re-cost is marginal, not strict: E1 is landed and documented in git, so re-entering arg-resolution later reads from a recorded change, not from fading memory. A dozen lines against a documented, sound extension point is cheap whenever it lands — so deferral does not impose a real penalty that would justify building speculatively now.
args.author: maint-bot

args.text: Wiring convenience does not override layering. mu's charter is explicit: 'mu is the executor; ordering is the DAG's job.' Putting an after: ordering primitive inside ewe bodies places sequencing in the wrong layer — the design's own stated preference is 'dataflow preferred', not in-body ordering.
args.author: maint-bot

args.text: Convergence's design is open and unimplemented — there is NO concrete consumer, so the exact ordering shape it will need is unknown. Building a guessed primitive now risks building the wrong gate; a known-cheap step toward an unknown target is still speculation about the target.
args.author: hist-bot

args.text: The DAG path is not free for the author: two separate mu actions require explicit output-wiring between them. The after: field expresses the same ordering in one ewe body with no wiring ceremony, so it is not mere duplication — it is a cheaper authoring surface for an intra-body sequence.
args.author: shipper-bot

args.text: Not pure speculation: convergence IS on the roadmap and the E1 change makes the gate trivial right now. Skipping a near-free, sound primitive that a known-upcoming model needs is not YAGNI — it is deferring a guaranteed-cheap step into a guaranteed-costlier future touch.
args.author: shipper-bot

args.text: Deferring is not free: doing it now is trivial precisely because the E1 arg-resolution change is fresh in hand. Adding it later means re-entering that code cold after E1 context has faded, re-deriving soundness — a strictly higher cost than the dozen lines now.
args.author: shipper-bot

args.text: The gate is cheap to add LATER, when a concrete convergence consumer actually appears (the E1 change keeps it ~a dozen lines whenever it lands). Deferring loses nothing: the ergonomic 'converge; notify in one body' shape can be introduced exactly when convergence is designed, not speculatively in v1.
args.author: maint-bot

args.text: Convergence may later want a tight 'converge; notify' sequence inside ONE ewe body for ergonomics, rather than the ceremony of two separate mu actions plus output-wiring between them. Cutting the gate forces that worse-ergonomics shape on the convergence author.
args.author: shipper-bot

args.text: Pure ordering only becomes necessary in convergence models (e.g. #Converge then #Notify 'done'). Convergence is scoped out of v1 and its design is open/unimplemented — there is no concrete convergence consumer yet. Building the gate now is speculative (YAGNI).
args.author: hist-bot

args.text: mu's DAG already orders independent actions by dependency. Two ordered-but-independent effects can be two separate mu actions, which the DAG sequences for free. An after: field duplicates the DAG and creates two overlapping ordering mechanisms — against mu's charter ('ordering is the DAG's job') and the design's stated 'dataflow preferred'.
args.author: maint-bot

args.text: Position B: Build the after:/callReady gate in v1. It is cheap now (~a dozen lines on top of the just-landed E1 change) and closes the ordering gap before convergence needs it.
args.author: shipper-bot

args.text: Position A: Cut pure ordering from v1. v1 is observe-only; data-dependency ordering already sequences every effect chain. No A-before-B-without-dataflow shape occurs.
args.author: maint-bot

args.text: Should ewe build a pure-ordering primitive (after:/callReady gate sequencing A-before-B without dataflow) in v1, or cut it?
args.author: chazu
